# The Analysis Dashboard {#sec-tech-dashboard}

The dashboard is the app's deepest module nesting (@sec-arch-nested) and its only
purely app-owned persistence. This chapter covers the three tiers and
`app/logic/analysis_store.R`.

## Three tiers {#sec-tech-dash-tiers}

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-tech-dash
%%| fig-cap: "The dashboard's three tiers and their database-backed store."
flowchart TD
  T3["analysis_dashboard.R<br/><b>Tier 3</b> — lists Analyses, add/navigate"]
  T2["analysis_dashboard/group.R<br/><b>Tier 2</b> — one Analysis, its Plot boxes"]
  T1["analysis_dashboard/item.R<br/><b>Tier 1</b> — one saved Plot (value box + thumbnail)"]
  T3 -- "1 per Analysis" --> T2
  T2 -- "1 per saved Plot" --> T1
  T3 -. reads/writes .-> S[("phylotrace_analyses<br/>phylotrace_plots")]
  T1 -. reopen/restore .-> V["Visualization tab"]
```

The dashboard bubbles two requests up to `main.R` — `request_add_plot` and
`request_open_plot` — which route to the Visualization tab to create or restore a
plot (@sec-arch-signals, @sec-tech-viz-save).

## Persistence {#sec-tech-dash-store}

State is not held in memory: Analyses and their Plots live in the database
(`app/logic/analysis_store.R`) in two `phylotrace_` tables, so they are
automatically scoped to their database and travel with the file:

```{.r filename="app/logic/analysis_store.R"}
"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS phylotrace_analyses (
   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, description TEXT,
   created TEXT NOT NULL, modified TEXT NOT NULL,
   isolate_selection TEXT, isolate_universe TEXT )",
"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS phylotrace_plots (
   id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, analysis_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
   name TEXT NOT NULL, plot_type TEXT NOT NULL,
   inputs_json TEXT, thumb_b64 TEXT, created TEXT NOT NULL, modified TEXT NOT NULL )"
```

The store follows the app's standard idiom — a private connection closed on exit,
parameterised statements — and is created lazily (`ensure_schema()`, which also
runs `ALTER TABLE` to add later columns to an older database). Its API is a clean
CRUD surface: `list_analyses()`, `add_analysis()`, `rename_analysis()`,
`update_analysis_settings()`, `delete_analysis()` (which cascades to child plots);
and `list_plots()`, `get_plot()`, `upsert_plot()`, `duplicate_plot()`,
`rename_plot()`, `delete_plot()`.

::: {.callout-important title="What a saved plot stores — and why list_plots() omits it"}
A Plot row stores its `plot_type`, the full input snapshot as `inputs_json`, and a
base64 PNG `thumb_b64`. The JSON is what makes a plot **restorable** — reopening
feeds it straight back into a fresh Visualization tab of the right type. The
thumbnail is what makes the dashboard **fast**: `list_plots()` deliberately omits
the heavy `inputs_json` body and returns only the thumbnails, so a dashboard of
many plots renders quickly and the full snapshot is read only when a plot is
actually reopened. Adding `inputs_json` back into the listing query would regress
that.
:::

## Selection and universe {#sec-tech-dash-selection}

An Analysis records both a static isolate `selection` and the isolate `universe` it
was created against. `selection_differs()` compares selections ignoring order, and
`list_isolates()` reads the current non-reference isolate pool — so the dashboard
can tell when the database has grown or changed under a saved Analysis and
reconcile its selection accordingly.

The whole dashboard refreshes on the shared revision bus rather than a bespoke
signal, so saving a plot from the Visualization tab, or importing new isolates,
updates the dashboard without a manual reload (@sec-arch-signals).

## Chapter summary

- Three nested modules: Analyses (Tier 3) → one Analysis (Tier 2) → one saved Plot
  (Tier 1), the lower two instantiated once per row.
- `analysis_store.R` is the CRUD surface over `phylotrace_analyses`/
  `phylotrace_plots`, created lazily and migrated with `ALTER TABLE`.
- A Plot stores type, `inputs_json` (restorable) and a thumbnail (fast listing);
  the listing query must not read the JSON.
- The dashboard stays in sync via the revision bus, not a bespoke signal.
